newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban send delegation to Iran.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban send delegation to Iran.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban militia has sent a delegation to neighbouring Iran in what diplomats said might be an attempt to improve strained ties.
Mullah Haqqani, a Taleban spokesman in the southern city of Kandahar, said the delegation, led by acting Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammed Ghous, was in Herat en route for Tehran.
He did not disclose the purpose of the mission, which follows an Iranian offer to host peace talks among warring Afghan factions, including the Taleban.
Haqqani said the Taleban had not been formally notified of the Iranian offer, made by Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister for Asia-Pacific Affairs Alaeddin Boroujerdi at the weekend.
The English-language Tehran Times on Sunday quoted Boroujerdi as saying that any peace plan evolved without the participation of all Afghan factions was doomed to fail.

He said the Taleban were among factions expected to take part in the proposed Tehran talks. "Necessary coordinations have been made in this regard, but the exact dates have not been fixed yet," the paper quoted him as saying.
A spokesman for General Abdul Rashid Dostum, a key member of an anti-Taleban alliance, also said no formal invitation to the Iranian-sponsored talks had arrived.
A U.N. official said the proposed meeting in Tehran was not part of a U.N. negotiating process, although Iran has said in the past that it supports U.N.-led peace efforts.
U.N. special envoy to Afghanistan Norbert Holl brought representatives of the Taleban and their foes together for three days of talks that ended inconclusively in Islamabad last week.
The two sides agreed to meet again next month to discuss a ceasefire, an exchange of prisoners and other issues.
The next day the Taleban launched an assault north of Kabul, capturing Bagram military airbase and the town of Charikar.
On Monday the militia said it was ready for more talks with Dostum and former government commander Ahmad Shah Masood, but rejected a key opposition demand for the demilitarisation of Kabul.
